nodes.description: Radial sorting is the developmental step in which Schwann cells segregate large-calibre axons out of bundles into 1:1 relationships before myelinating them. Mouse work places MTMR5's main peripheral-nerve role here rather than in myelin maintenance: Mtmr5-null nerves contain fewer myelinated axons and show sorting defects, while Mtmr13 loss produces the outfoldings. Whether this division of labour holds in human CMT4B3, where outfoldings are seen, is unresolved - see the model-mismatch discussion below.

evidence.snippet: MTMR5 consistently increased MTMR2 phosphatase activity 4.6- and 3.4-fold for PI(3)P and phosphatidylinositol 3,5-bisphosphate, respectively (data not shown).

nodes.description: ATP production, oxygen consumption and glycolytic output were reduced, consistent with metabolic quiescence. Mitochondrial mass, respiratory-chain assembly and mtDNA copy number were preserved in these cells, in contrast to the reduced mtDNA content measured in this patient's muscle. These are observations in R763H/G1064E fibroblasts from one patient. The original variants were classified as uncertain and likely benign, and genetic rescue was not performed; attribution to SBF1 and extrapolation to nerve remain provisional.

evidence.reference_title: Mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic quiescence and premature senescence in CMT4B3 fibroblasts.
evidence.snippet: Patient fibroblasts exhibited fragmented mitochondrial networks with a shift toward fission, together with reduced ATP production, while mitochondrial mass, respiratory chain assembly, and markers of mitochondrial biogenesis were preserved.

nodes.description: Glutathione was reduced across four SBF1 patient fibroblast lines without increased basal mitochondrial or cytosolic ROS. Most lines showed increased oxidant-induced cell death, but line 946 was more resistant than controls. Thus depletion and oxidant sensitivity were not uniformly coupled.

evidence.reference_title: Charcot Marie Tooth disease pathology is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and lower glutathione production.
evidence.snippet: the level of GSH in the fibroblasts with CMT4B3 associated mutations is significantly lower than in control fibroblasts

experimental_models.description: Direct biochemical readout in four patient lines.
experimental_models.name: Four SBF1 patient fibroblast lines with redox assays

nodes.description: The four-patient-line study found reduced NADPH estimates. Lower pentose-phosphate pathway substrate availability was proposed, but pathway flux was not directly measured and G6PDH activity was largely preserved.

evidence.snippet: In contrast to the NADH pool, the level of NADPH in the patients’ cells was significantly lower

nodes.description: Fibroblasts from the British index case homozygous for c.5477_5478del showed markedly reduced MTMR5 protein. Heterozygous parental fibroblasts had levels comparable to controls. This directly supports protein loss for this frameshift context and does not establish loss of MTMR2 protein.

evidence.reference_title: A novel frameshift deletion in autosomal recessive SBF1-related syndromic neuropathy with necklace fibres.
evidence.snippet: Functional analysis showed a markedly reduced level of MTMR5 protein encoded by SBF1 in the index case.

experimental_models.name: British frameshift patient and parental fibroblasts

nodes.description: Adult Mtmr5-null sciatic nerves contained approximately 10% fewer myelinated axons, with normal myelin thickness and no outfoldings. Reduced myelinated counts do not by themselves establish axonal degeneration or slowed conduction.
nodes.id: Reduced Myelinated Axon Number in Mouse Nerve

evidence.reference_title: Distinct roles for the Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease-causing endosomal regulators Mtmr5 and Mtmr13 in axon radial sorting and Schwann cell myelination.
evidence.snippet: Loss of Mtmr5 in mice did not cause CMT4B-like myelin outfoldings. However, adult Mtmr5-/- mouse nerves contained fewer myelinated axons than control nerves, likely as a result of axon radial sorting defects.

evidence.reference_title: SET binding factor 1 (SBF1) mutation causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4B3.
evidence.snippet: We suggest that the compound heterozygous mutations in SBF1 are the underlying causes of a novel CMT4B subtype, designated as CMT4B3.

evidence.reference_title: Bi-allelic variants in MTMR5/SBF1 cause Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4B3 featuring mitochondrial dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: these variants were classified as “uncertain” (evidence of pathogenicity: PM2, PP3) and “likely benign”, respectively

evidence.reference_title: SBF1 mutations associated with autosomal recessive axonal neuropathy with cranial nerve involvement.
evidence.snippet: this variant was in cis with c.2209_2210del, which causes a premature stop codon 994 amino acids upstream.

nodes.description: Patient fibroblasts showed approximately 5.46-fold increased AKT Ser473/total AKT, while Thr308/total AKT was unchanged. This is partial, noncanonical activation rather than proof of globally increased AKT kinase signalling. These are observations in R763H/G1064E fibroblasts from one patient. The original variants were classified as uncertain and likely benign, and genetic rescue was not performed; attribution to SBF1 and extrapolation to nerve remain provisional.

evidence.reference_title: Mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic quiescence and premature senescence in CMT4B3 fibroblasts.
evidence.snippet: AKT phosphorylation at Ser473 was increased in the absence of complete canonical AKT activation.

nodes.description: Both Spanish brothers had bilateral hearing loss. Brainstem auditory evoked potentials in the index patient specifically supported left sensorineural cochlear impairment; that localization should not be generalized to every affected ear or family.

evidence.reference_title: SBF1 mutations associated with autosomal recessive axonal neuropathy with cranial nerve involvement.
evidence.snippet: auditory evoked potentials were consistent with left sensorineural cochlear impairment

nodes.description: CRISPR deletion of the mtmr5 gene, with absence of transcript verified by RT-PCR; suitable protein antibodies were unavailable. From ten days post-fertilization, body length and absolute brain length/height are reduced by roughly 10%. Brain-to-body proportions remain similar. Seven-day larvae have increased axonal branching and shorter branches; fourteen-day lateral-line nerves show axon-myelin detachment. Larval motor assays did not show a swimming deficit. Brain-enriched transcriptomic changes are associations, not proof of a neurogenesis defect.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of a novel zebrafish model of MTMR5-associated Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4B3.
evidence.snippet: Overall, our mtmr5 knockout zebrafish mirror genetic, clinical and pathologic features of human Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4B3.
